us-gaap:ProfitLoss is consolidated NI. us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss is NI attributable to common stock in these PWR filings. Consolidated CFO includes all controlled subsidiaries; minority distributions are retained separately. Do not pair consolidated CFO with attributable NI without naming the different bases.

Company FCF = CFO - cash PP&E purchases + PP&E sale and related insurance proceeds. Analyst gross-PPE FCF excludes those proceeds; the after-SBC proxy deducts SBC but is not owner earnings. FY2025 also spent 103.370 million on an asset acquisition outside the PP&E capex row. Keep that amount and business acquisitions separate and visible. Maintenance capex, normalized working capital and economic dilution costs are not established.

9M2026 cash-flow contribution from contract liabilities was +1983.686 million versus +124.823 million in 9M2025; contract asset/receivable cash uses also rose. Such timing-dependent advance/milestone funding must not be mechanically annualized. Subtracting this single liability inflow is a sensitivity, not a normalized earnings estimate.
Separate cash software capex is not identified in reviewed statements. Keep it null, not zero; do not invent an amount or double count it within PP&E.

Balance sheets report noncontrolling interests in permanent equity. No separately identified redeemable NCI or preferred stock line was found in the reviewed statements. Those fields remain null rather than an invented zero. Total assets = liabilities + permanent total equity at each covered year/quarter end; the unclassified equity residual is separately calculated as a check.

Current balance-sheet debt includes short-term borrowing, where applicable (8.710 million at June 2026); the long-term debt note total excludes that short-term borrowing. Current plus noncurrent carrying debt includes finance leases and lease-financing obligations as reported, but excludes operating leases and contingent acquisition consideration. Keep operating leases and contingent consideration separate to avoid hiding commitments or double counting debt.
